title: Observability roundtrip adapter for structured log joins and cross-tenant correlation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an adapter component that preserves and surfaces correlation metadata across the entire log ingestion path (edge -> relay -> storage) and enables efficient 'roundtrip' joins between traces, metrics, and structured logs without rehydration. The adapter will normalize KV payloads, materialize lightweight correlation anchors, and add join hints for downstream Loki/ELK indexing and query-time joins.
background: We currently have ad-hoc correlation propagation in sidecars and some Loki ingesters, but queries that join logs to traces or metrics are expensive or unreliable when tenant-specific fields are renamed or when logs traverse different transport encodings. Past tickets focused on schema enforcement and correlation ID propagation, but we still see: 1) inconsistent KV keys across clients, 2) expensive reingest/rehydration during cross-source joins, 3) fanout duplication without deterministic anchors. This ticket defines a stable adapter to fix those issues for the next Observability sprint.
goals: Provide a protocol-agnostic adapter that normalizes structured log KV keys and emits canonical correlation anchors
Ensure anchors are stable across tenant sharding and remain queryable without full log-body rehydration
Add lightweight join hints to log metadata so downstream query engines (Loki/ELK) can perform efficient joins to traces/metrics
Reduce cross-system join latency by >40% on representative dashboards and reduce duplicated fanout by 20%
scope: Relay transformation plugin to materialize correlation anchors into top-level labels/fields
Indexing hints for Loki compatible label set and ELK ingest pipeline mapping
End-to-end integration test harness and dashboarding to validate join latency improvements
out_of_scope: Changing downstream query engine internals (no changes to Loki core),
Shiping a fully-managed cross-tenant trace store (only join optimization via anchors)
Rewriting legacy clients — instead, provide shims and migration guidance
acceptance_criteria: Adapter accepts JSON/JSONL and protobuf-encoded structured logs and outputs normalized envelope
Canonical anchor fields present as top-level labels in Loki-compatible output for 99% of synthetic test cases
Cross-system join benchmark (sample dashboard) shows >=40% reduction in median latency versus baseline
Fanout duplicate rate decreased by >=20% for multi-sink pipelines under the test harness
Security checklist completed: KMS keys used for any anchor obfuscation where tenant-sensitive fields are present
design_notes: Use a deterministic key canonicalization map with tenant-specific prefixes to avoid collisions
Materialize 'corr_anchor' as a compact stable hash plus optional human-readable tag (corr_anchor_hash, corr_anchor_tag)
Keep original payload intact in a compressed store for forensic rehydration when needed, but avoid using it for routine joins
Expose adapter config as a Relay plugin with feature flags for gradual rollout per-tenant
Backpressure: if normalization fails or mapping table unavailable, forward original envelope with a 'normalization:skip' label and emit metric for operator action
implementation_steps: 1) Define canonical keymap and hashing scheme (TL;DR spec in Confluence)
2) Implement edge-side normalization library (Go) with conn pool and low-latency path
3) Add Relay plugin that materializes corr_anchor labels and join hints into output envelope
4) Extend Loki ingest adapter mapping to lift corr_anchor to label space and add index-time hints
5) Build integration test harness to replay production sampling through the adapter and measure join latency
6) Create migration runbook and feature flags for per-tenant enablement
7) Open PRs for code, tests, and configuration; iterate on perf/observability feedback
migration_plan: Start with a canary tenant set (<=5 tenants) using feature flag. Run adapter in parallel mode where Relay emits both original envelope and normalized envelope with corr_anchor labels for a week. Monitor duplicate counts, join latency, and error rates. If metrics stable and acceptance criteria met, flip flag to forward-only for additional tenants in cohorts.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal canary with synthetic load (2 days). Phase 1: 5 beta tenants (2 weeks). Phase 2: expand to high-volume tenants with real dashboards and tracing hooks enabled (4 weeks). Provide automated rollback if duplicate rate or error rate exceeds thresholds defined in the runbook.
test_plan: Unit tests for canonical keymap and hashing determinism
Property tests for no-loss normalization roundtrip
Load test of Relay + adapter using sampled production traces to validate latency and duplicate metrics
End-to-end query tests joining logs to traces and metrics verifying correctness and latency improvements
Security test: tenant field obfuscation and KMS key rotation test
risks: Incorrect canonicalization causing join mismatches across older clients
Increased index cardinality in Loki if too many unique anchor labels are materialized — mitigate via bucketing
Backpressure leading to dropped logs if normalization becomes a bottleneck — mitigations: async fallback and metrics
Privacy leakage if non-approved tenant fields are promoted to labels — gating via config and KMS obfuscation
